core.title: Bind every required telemetry item to its emitting source
core.given: An acceptance decision in the repository (changed or not) has telemetry disposition required and lists a resolvable concrete telemetry URN (a required item)
core.when: the repository's acceptance decisions and non-test implementation source are in that state, regardless of which files the current change touches
core.then: Bind the required item to at least one non-test implementation source file with the profile's telemetry binding construct naming the required item's exact URN, resolved the way the telemetry source-binding rule defines.
prefer: Put the telemetry binding construct naming the required item's exact URN in the non-test implementation source file that actually emits the item; the binding must resolve the way the telemetry source-binding rule of this family defines — fix resolution failures under that rule.
If nothing emits the item, drop the requirement from the acceptance decision instead of inventing a binding.
avoid: Binding the required item only from a test file — bindings in test files do not count as implementation.
Adding a telemetry binding to source that does not emit the item just to silence the finding.
Leaving a required item no source claims: telemetry the plan believes in and the code has never heard of.
unless: The repository has not yet adopted the telemetry rule family — the rule is inert until adoption, like every rule in this family.
core.why: Traceability needs all three legs — planned, implemented, tested; this rule closes the implemented leg so a required item is never planned yet unemitted.
evidence: This rule's validator reports no finding: every required item has a resolved telemetry binding in non-test implementation source.
Reviewer can point, for each required URN of every acceptance decision, to the non-test implementation source file whose binding names it, or to the removal of the requirement.
verification: Required items: concrete telemetry URNs collected from acceptance decisions whose telemetry disposition is required.

Implementation bindings: every resolved telemetry binding in non-test implementation source, with no directory restriction of its own — the source-to-telemetry edge resolved by the telemetry source-binding rule.

Finding = required items minus implementation bindings, computed over the whole scanned repository; report it at the tracking-plan item's own file — the plan artifact that tracks the required telemetry item itself, which is not established to be the artifact recording the acceptance decision — because that is where the remedy starts (bind the emitting source or stop requiring what nothing emits).
An unresolvable required URN is the acceptance-decision rule's finding and is not double-reported here.
Fix-hint shape: the emitting source file followed by the telemetry binding that names the required item (or drop the requirement); the concrete example is realization provenance only.
Inert until the telemetry rule family is adopted.
Severity 2; disposition strict — the check fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: acceptance state: telemetry disposition required with at least one resolvable concrete telemetry URN
non-test implementation source (any directory; test files excluded)
validator finding of this rule: required item with no implementation binding

fires: An existing acceptance decision with required telemetry disposition lists a concrete URN and no non-test implementation source file carries a resolved telemetry binding naming it — even if the current change touches no source.
An acceptance-only change adds a required concrete URN that no non-test implementation source binds.
The only telemetry binding naming a required URN sits in a test file.
The emitting source is removed or its telemetry binding is deleted while the acceptance still requires the item.
doesNotFire: The repository has not adopted the telemetry rule family (rule is inert).
The acceptance's telemetry disposition is not required.
The required URN is unresolvable — that is the acceptance-decision rule's finding, not this one's.
At least one non-test implementation source file, in any directory, already binds the required item via a resolved telemetry binding.

neutralityNotes: The `// Telemetry:` binding syntax has no vocabulary key, so urn.binding.telemetry is proposed and required from the profile; the core says only 'the profile's telemetry binding construct'. No authoritative telemetry URN pattern exists in bun.json: required items are matched by the exact URN listed in the acceptance decision, not by a namespace shape, so no urn.telemetry key is required or proposed; the single concrete URN from the fix hint is one application-specific example and stays Bun-side provenance (bunOnly, verifier_detail[4]). The reporting target is preserved exactly: findings report at the tracking-plan item's own file, stated neutrally as the plan artifact that tracks the required telemetry item itself; the core explicitly does not equate it with the artifact recording the acceptance decision, and the profile supplies only the plan-artifact kind ('tracking plan') via roles.plan_artifact.kinds — the reporting obligation itself is rule-specific and lives in core verification. References to the companion rule (coder.bun.telemetry-source-binding) and this rule's validator (bun_telemetry_code) are realization ids: the core names them generically ('the telemetry source-binding rule', 'this rule's validator') and keeps the concrete ids in bunOnly. The strict-disposition policy node names the atdd-bun tool; the core keeps the policy (fail on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline) without the tool name, and per-rule severity 2 stays with the rule in core verification. The application-specific fix-hint example (path, header, URN) and the exact Bun profile values live only in bun.json, which remains the delivered reference realization. Sidecar-only scaffolding (audit, trace, additions, sharedNodes) was not itemized and is not part of the core.
